standard.description: This standard prescribes the technical requirements, chemical parameters, active-matter thresholds, analytical testing procedures, and toxicological limits for sodium alpha olefin sulphonate (AOS) used as a high-performance surfactant in cosmetics, household synthetic detergents (liquid, paste, or powder), and other industrial surface-active formulations.

certification.description: Voluntary Certification under the Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS). However, manufacturers are highly encouraged to apply for a license to print the prestigious BIS 'Standard Mark' (ISI Mark) on product drums and shipping containers as a certified guarantee of chemical purity and low-sultone safety. This is governed by the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 1986 and the rules and regulations framed thereunder.
requirements: Sodium Alpha Olefin Sulphonate (AOS) is classified into three distinct physical forms: Type 1 (Powder or flakes), Type 2 (Paste), and Type 3 (Liquid), each characterized by unique active matter and moisture limits.
Mandates that the active ingredient (percent by mass, minimum) shall be: Type 1 (90 percent), Type 2 (64 percent), and Type 3 (37 percent), quantitatively determined by standard titration.
Moisture content is restricted to a maximum of 3.0 percent by mass for Type 1 (powder or flakes) to maintain physical free-flowing stability and prevent caking.
Limits unreacted free alpha olefins (percent by mass, maximum) to: Type 1 (3.0 percent), Type 2 (3.0 percent), and Type 3 (1.5 percent), extracted using petroleum ether (boiling range 40°C to 60°C).
Restricts free alkalinity to: Type 1 (0.5 percent), Type 2 (0.5 percent), and Type 3 (0.2 percent) by mass maximum, to prevent skin irritation.
Specifies that the colour of a 5 percent active matter solution, matched in a 4-cm cell using a No. 42 filter in a Klett colorimeter, shall not exceed 100 matched slides.

Specifies that the colour of a 5 percent active matter solution, matched in a 5.25 inch cell in a Lovibond tintometer, shall not exceed 12 Lovibond units (expressed as the sum of yellow + five times red slides, Y+5R).

Under active Amendment No. 4 (May 2020), Table 1, Sl No. (v), col 2 is updated to insert 'Or' between 'a)' and 'b)' to clarify that either the Klett or Lovibond colour matching method may be utilized.

Restricts total inorganic salts (such as sodium sulphate, determined via alcohol-insoluble residues dried at 105°C) to: Type 1 (6.0 percent), Type 2 (3.0 percent), and Type 3 (3.0 percent) by mass maximum.

Restricts disulphonates to a maximum of 6.0 percent (on 100 percent active basis) for all three types, determined by High Performance Liquid Chromatography (HPLC) with a Refractive Index Detector (RID).

Under active Amendment No. 1 (October 2007), because gamma sultone is an extremely potent skin sensitizer, its maximum concentration is strictly restricted to 70 ppb (parts per billion) on a 100 percent active basis (substituting 'ppb' in place of the erroneous 'ppm' in Table 1).
Restricts total sultones to a maximum of 200 ppm and internal (delta) sultones to a maximum of 50 ppm on a 100 percent active basis.
Surfactants must achieve rapid biodegradation, passing the standard Modified Sturm Test in accordance with IS 13933.
Under active Amendment No. 3 (March 2015), the material must pass skin irritation and sensitization safety evaluations conducted in accordance with IS 11601 : 2002.

Each package must be legibly and indelibly marked with: name, brand, source of manufacture, net mass, batch number, month/year of manufacture, and the mandatory warning: '(CAUTION: DO NOT USE CHLORINE BLEACH ALONG WITH THIS PRODUCT)' to prevent the formation of highly toxic chlorinated sultones.
Observed or calculated test or analytical values must be rounded off mathematically in accordance with IS 2 : 1960 to match the significant places of the specified limits.
